housing.summary: Turin is a comparatively affordable major-Italian-city rental market; a 1-bedroom apartment in the city centre is cited at roughly EUR 700-950/month (Numbeo lists a central 1-bed at about EUR 771/month; HousingAnywhere cites an overall average near EUR 940). The main online rental portals are Immobiliare.it and Idealista.it. Italian law does not impose a single national deposit cap as in Switzerland; the security deposit (cauzione) is customary and typically ranges from 1 to 3 months' rent, commonly up to 3.

banking.summary: A newcomer opens a conto corrente (bank account) in person at a local branch. Typical documents required: a valid passport/national ID, an Italian codice fiscale (tax code), proof of address/residence in Italy, and for non-EU nationals a valid permesso di soggiorno (residence permit). Major banks with a strong Turin presence include Intesa Sanpaolo (headquartered in Turin) and UniCredit. Note: a single authoritative source page for the exact document checklist was not verified, so this block is flagged source_missing.
required_docs: Proof of address / residence in Italy
Residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) for non-EU nationals

schools.summary: International schooling in Turin is anchored by the International School of Turin (IST), an authorised IB World School since 1963 offering the full IB Continuum (PYP, MYP, IB Diploma) in English (https://www.isturin.it/). A directory of international schools in and around Turin is maintained at https://www.international-schools-database.com/in/turin.

legal_admin.summary: On moving to Turin a newcomer must file a 'dichiarazione di residenza' (declaration of residence) with the Comune di Torino civil-registry office (Anagrafe) within 20 days of taking up residence; non-EU nationals must also hold a valid permesso di soggiorno (residence permit). The municipality then completes the anagrafic registration.
legal_admin.registration_step: File a 'dichiarazione di residenza' with the Comune di Torino Anagrafe (civil registry) within 20 days of taking up residence; non-EU nationals must also hold a valid permesso di soggiorno

tax_finance.summary: Individuals need a codice fiscale (Italian tax identification code), issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate. EU and non-EU foreign citizens applying for their first codice fiscale must book an in-person appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office; in Turin this is handled by the Direzione Provinciale di Torino. The code identifies the taxpayer to the Italian tax authority.

transport.summary: Public transport in Turin is operated by Gruppo Torinese Trasporti (GTT). The current official monthly urban ('Formula U') pass price could not be verified from an official GTT source (the GTT tariff pages returned an error), so monthly_pass_price is left null rather than invented. Driving: EU/EEA licences remain valid in Italy; a non-EU licence holder may drive for up to one year from acquiring residenza anagrafica, after which the licence must be exchanged (only where a reciprocity agreement with Italy exists) or an Italian licence obtained by examination (https://www.esteri.it/en/servizi-opportunita/italiani-all-estero/autoveicoli_e_patenti/patenteguida/). Healthcare: new residents access public healthcare by registering with the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN) at the local ASL and choosing a medico di base (family doctor); those resident under three months generally cannot enrol.
